test_title: PYST 41 - SSC CHSL 2025 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 27 Nov, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: A can complete a task in 10 days, while B can finish the same task in 12 days. They decide to work alternately, with A starting the work on the first day. How many days will it take for them to complete the entire task?
solution:
**Given:**

A = 10 days

B = 12 days

**Formula Used:**

Work = Efficiency × Time

Total Work = LCM of given times

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total Work = LCM of 10 and 12 = 60 units

⇒ Efficiency of A = 60 ÷ 10 = 6 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of B = 60 ÷ 12 = 5 units/day

⇒ Work done in 2 days (A + B) = 6 + 5 = 11 units

⇒ Work done in 10 days (5 cycles) = 11 × 5 = 55 units

⇒ Remaining Work = 60 − 55 = 5 units

⇒ Next turn is A

⇒ Time taken by A to complete 5 units = 5 ÷ 6 = 5/6 day

⇒ Total time = 10 + 5/6 = 10.83 days 

**∴ The correct answer is 10.83 days.**
